items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: We all quit to a man. It was Freeman and the whole band.

ctx.x: And he loved this music. There was a fascination between us. We liked each other. And he didn't like what was happening to between Wingy and me. He kept telling me that Wingy was just taking me. I was paying for my musical education, is what he was saying. And of course, in the El Dorado Club after that, we were still together, but this thing was going on underneath.

And it was at the El Dorado that Wingy got into an argument with the boss. And the boss grabbed him and tore his false arm off and threw it across the floor. Arm and coat. And Wingy got up to the band and he says, let's go. We all quit to a man. It was Freeman and the whole band. Krupa -- I know Krupa and Freeman were in that band together. We played the floor show, we played everything. And it was a great experience, great band.
So it was about that time that I decided I would go live with Bill, because I didn't -- I was beginning to get fascinated with living with him. And that style, that I could

items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: Art Hodes called me from Chicago

ctx.x: The point is, it happened to you and if it had been one of those that happened so fast that you didn't know anything about it, but you had a few seconds.

Well, I was very lucky. I had no ill effects from it. The first show I did, I didn't do anything for seven months, and Art Hodes called me from Chicago -- he had that wonderful show, I think it was called Blues Alley. And he asked me if I'd come out. And the doctor said now you might feel some pain when you start to play again, because the expansion and all, but there was nothing. No pain, it was marvelous and I played that first thing and that started me all over again.
You mean you actually hadn't blown, you hadn't played at all.
